A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two dogs presented with a progressive leukodystrophy characterized by multifocal areas of myelin degeneration and oligodendrocyte hyperplasia.
oligodendrocyte dysfunction is a common cause of inherited myelin disorders in animals.
oligodendrocyte dysplasia is a progressive neurologic disorder of young-adult Bullmastiff dogs that has similarities to the Charolais syndrome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oligodendrocytes can undergo dysplasia, and that oligodendrogliosis can cause a leukodystrophic disorder in dogs, as well as cattle.
